summary: DECISION 1 is HALF decided, and the half that is not decided is the one DB-012 and ORG-007 were about to build on. WFC-004 created the canonical vendor identity — `public.vendor_entities` — and created NEITHER `vendors` NOR `org_vendors`, because whether those two names are one entity is UNPROVEN and CP-096 forbids guessing it. DB-012 (vendor-to-organization ownership) and ORG-007 (canonical vendor services) must not proceed to author vendor identity or vendor-to-organization ownership until the merge question is settled, because they would be authoring on top of a decision nobody has made.

what_was_decided_and_why.the_shape: The VEND-102 contract, field for field, in `public.vendor_entities`: id, org_id NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations ON DELETE CASCADE, legal_name, display_name, normalized_legal_name, category (the 8-value VEND-102 vocabulary), status (the 8-value VEND-102 vocabulary), city, region, country, external_accounting_id, primary_contact_name/email/phone, merged_into_id (composite same-org FK, ON DELETE RESTRICT), created_by, updated_by, created_at, updated_at. Plus `public.vendor_entity_aliases` as the real target for `VendorMergePlan.aliasesToRetain` (lib/admin/vendor-identity.ts:292-346), whose column shape is exactly what that function emits.
what_was_decided_and_why.the_evidence_for_the_shape: It is the ONLY vendor table in this repository with a reviewed ADR (docs/admin-feature-specs/adr/VEND-102-vendor-identity-deduplication.md), a tested pure implementation, archived DDL and a verify function. `VendorIdentityRecord` (:93-109) matches that archived DDL field for field, and `buildVendorIdentityRow` (:126-146) produces rows in that shape. `buildVendorIdentityRow`, `planVendorMerge` and `findVendorDuplicateMatches` have ZERO production callers — only the test — so the storage gap is real, not merely unused.
what_was_decided_and_why.the_evidence_for_the_NAME_proven_by_exec: Creating the relation as `vendors` would BREAK the one CP-098-correct reader among the seven. `app/api/admin/vendors/route.ts:21` selects `id, organization_id, name, vendor_type, rating, created_at, updated_at`; against the VEND-102 shape that select raises SQLSTATE 42703 `column "organization_id" does not exist` (measured). 42703 is not 42P01, so the route's branch at :31 does not fire, and the outer catch's `msg.includes("relation") && msg.includes("does not exist")` at :56 does not fire either, because a 42703 message contains 'does not exist' but NOT 'relation'. The route would return 503 'Vendors unavailable' instead of today's honest `{success:true, vendors:[], unavailable:true, unavailableReason:"Vendors table not yet migrated."}`. The archived `logistics_vendors` shape (20260605100000) — the only other candidate in the repository — ALSO raises 42703 against the same select, so no candidate was available and this was not a choice between two workable options.

what_is_UNRESOLVED_and_why_it_cannot_be_.the_question: Are `vendors` and `org_vendors` one entity or two?
why_the_repository_cannot_answer_it: The two READERS demand mutually exclusive tenant column names for the same relation name: `vendors` is read with `organization_id`, `org_vendors` with `org_id`. If both names are real DDL on some target they cannot be one table. That is a statement about the READERS.

NEITHER name has any DDL anywhere in this repository — not in the 315-file active chain, not in supabase/migrations/archive, not in supabase/migrations_backup, not in supabase/migration-archive/pre-reconciliation-local-only-2026-08-20. So there is no entity evidence to reason from.
DB-002 recorded that some hosted versions were applied by raw Management API SQL, so a target may hold either name and the chain cannot see it.

Three incompatible status vocabularies exist: `org_vendors`'s reader asks for 5 of the 7 non-'prospective' values of the VEND-102 status CHECK; archived `logistics_vendors` has no status column at all; `vendor_contracts.status` is {draft,active,expired,cancelled} and `event_vendor_requests.status` is {pending,confirmed,declined,cancelled}.
what_is_UNRESOLVED_and_why_it_cannot_be_.THE_ONE_QUERY_THAT_SETTLES_IT: select n.nspname, c.relname, c.relkind from pg_class c join pg_namespace n on n.oid = c.relnamespace where c.relname in ('vendors','org_vendors','vendor_compliance_documents','org_contracts','contract_signature_envelopes','vendor_aliases') order by 1,2;  — run read-only on ANY real target. relkind 'v' for `org_vendors` means it is a projection and the merge is settled as a view; relkind 'r' means it is a distinct entity and two masters are needed. Absent means the chain-absent premise still holds on that target.
what_is_UNRESOLVED_and_why_it_cannot_be_.why_no_view_was_created_under_either_nam: A view named `org_vendors` over `vendor_entities` would be a 3-line fix for one reader site, and creating it would RATIFY the merge CP-096 forbids. It was deliberately not created. If the product confirms the merge, that view is the remedy; if it refutes it, a second vendor master is needed and should be authored by the vendor-domain owner against an explicit column contract, not by widening this one.
what_is_UNRESOLVED_and_why_it_cannot_be_.and_two_relations_that_are_not_vendor_id: `org_contracts` and `contract_signature_envelopes` have NO archived DDL and NO ADR anywhere, and their readers want a contract lifecycle surface (`title`, `counterparty_name`, `expires_at`, `status`; and `status in (pending,sent)`, `created_at`). Unlike `vendors`/`org_vendors` there is not even a candidate to reconcile against, so these need a product owner and a column contract, not a database decision. `vendor_compliance_documents` is the SAME ENTITY as archived `vendor_documents` (20260720186000) under different column names — `expires_at` vs `expires_on`, `verification_status` vs `status` — so it is a duplicate projection whose canonical spelling is undecided.

what_the_receiver_must_do: DB-012 and ORG-007 read WFC-003's contract and then this handoff, and NEITHER may author vendor identity, a vendor-to-organization ownership rule, or a merge between `vendors` and `org_vendors` until the catalog query above has been run on a real target and its result recorded here.

The vendor-domain owner decides the `org_contracts` / `contract_signature_envelopes` column contract. Until then those two reader sites stay degraded, and the operator should be told that is the state rather than being shown a plausible zero.

The two VendorCategory vocabularies (8 values in lib/admin/vendor-identity.ts:8-17, 16 in lib/admin/vendor-domain.ts:23-26) are NOT reconciled. `vendor_entities.category` enforces the 8-value VEND-102 vocabulary; a vendor whose category exists only in the 16-value list cannot be written until a human says which is canonical. WFC-003 §5 item 15.
